summary: ListProviderFacts (internal/store/peloton.go) orders "workouts" family rows by the payload's own start_time field (newest first), not fetched_at (sync/write time), via a new providerFactDateField(family) lookup. Concurrent sync workers write rows in whatever order their HTTP requests complete, not the order the underlying events occurred in, so fetched_at-based ordering scrambled offline history's newest-first listing. Any future regen must keep offline history's underlying ListProviderFacts call ordering by start_time for "workouts"; families with no providerFactDateField entry keep the original fetched_at ordering unchanged (verified with a dedicated test), so this is additive, not a behavior change for every other family.
reason: MINOR #7 from a live post-fix verification sweep: offline history's dates appeared scrambled against a real ~3.5k-workout synced account. Root cause confirmed by reading ListProviderFacts's SQL directly -- ORDER BY fetched_at DESC, provider_id ASC, which reflects write order under a concurrency=4 worker pool, not the workouts' actual recorded dates.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck all green. New tests TestListProviderFacts_OrdersWorkoutsByStartTimeNotFetchOrder (writes rows oldest-start_time-first, confirms newest-first output despite write order) and TestListProviderFacts_UnaffectedFamiliesKeepFetchOrder (a family with no date field keeps fetched_at ordering). Live-verified against the user's real ~3.5k-workout account: `offline history --json` now returns strictly-decreasing start_time values across the first page.
